# Impeccable The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships. From your project root: ```bash npx impeccable install ``` Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). | Without Impeccable | With Impeccable | |---|---| | | | Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water. For a full project, see the [Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai): a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page. ## Why Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects. - **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target. - **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish). - **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key. Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see [Build something new](https://impeccable.style/docs/new-work) for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component: ``` /impeccable critique the pricing cards ``` ## How it works Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. [More on context files](https://impeccable.style/docs/context). Then name a command and a target: ``` /impeccable critique the onboarding flow /impeccable quieter the landing page /impeccable polish settings /impeccable harden checkout ``` Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut. ### 24 commands | | Commands | |---|---| | **Steer** | `bolder` amplifies safe designs · `quieter` tones down loud ones · `distill` removes what the page doesn't need · `colorize` brings color to a gray interface · `typeset` fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · `layout` fixes spacing and rhythm · `animate` adds transitions and interaction feedback · `delight` adds personality · `overdrive` goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects | | **Review** | `critique` is a scored UX review · `audit` is a technical quality report | | **Finish** | `polish` is the final pass before shipping · `harden` covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · `clarify` rewrites unclear copy · `adapt` handles screen sizes and devices · `optimize` fixes loading and rendering performance · `onboard` designs first-run flows and empty states | | **Iterate live** | `live` lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · `generate` produces variants of a named element without manual picking | | **Plan and set up** | `shape` plans UX before code · `init` writes `PRODUCT.md` · `document` writes `DESIGN.md` · `extract` pulls repeated patterns into your design system | The 24th, `craft`, is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type `/impeccable` alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). On Codex, open `/skills` or type `$impeccable` instead of the slash command. ### Live mode `/impeccable live` opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. [Iterate in the browser](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/iterate-live). Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your `package.json`'s optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo. ## Three ways to run the detector **In your agent.** The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. [Automatic design checks](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks). **In CI or your terminal.** The CLI needs no agent: ```bash npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge) npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description ``` Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: `npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173`. Exit code `2` means findings, `1` means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run `npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font"`. To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: ``. [Run a detector scan](https://impeccable.style/docs/detector) · [Configuration and ignores](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **In your browser.** The [Chrome extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/impeccable/bdkgmiklpdmaojlpflclinlofgjfpabf) overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. [Review with a visual overlay](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/critique-with-overlay). ## Installation ```bash npx impeccable install ``` The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. `npx impeccable update` refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass `--providers=claude,codex,cursor` and `--scope=project|global`. Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open `/hooks` and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run `/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once. [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness). Node is only needed for `npx`. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`.
Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`, then open `/plugin` and install Impeccable. **GitHub Copilot in VS Code:** install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable) or run `code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable`. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. [Details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md). **Grok Build:** `grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust` installs the skill, agents, and hook.
Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) ```bash git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor ``` Commit `.gitmodules`, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. To upgrade, run `git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable`, rerun the `link` command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass `--force`.
Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy `skills/impeccable` from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. | Tool | Repo folder | Global skills folder | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `.claude/` | `~/.claude/skills/` | | Cursor | `.cursor/` | | | Codex CLI, Replit Agent | `.agents/` | `~/.agents/skills/` | | Devin | `.devin/` | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `.github/` | | | Gemini CLI | `.gemini/` | | | Google Antigravity | `.agent/` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | | OpenCode | `.opencode/` | | | Grok Build | `.grok/` | `~/.grok/skills/` | | Hermes Agent | `.hermes/` | `${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/` | | DeepSeek Harness | `.dsh/` | `${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/` | | Pi | `.pi/` | | | Qoder | `.qoder/` | `~/.qoder/skills/` | | Rovo Dev | `.rovodev/` | `~/.rovodev/skills/` | | Mistral Vibe | `.vibe/` | `~/.vibe/skills/` | | Trae | `.trae/` | `~/.trae/skills/` | | Trae China | `.trae-cn/` | `~/.trae-cn/skills/` | For example: `mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/`. Notes: - A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run `npx impeccable install` to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path. - OpenCode also needs `.opencode/commands/impeccable.md` copied into your project's `.opencode/commands/` to provide `/impeccable`. - Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run `hermes skills trust` from the project root. Global installs need no trust step. - Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills) and [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/) skills docs. - Restart Trae after copying. - `impeccable install` and `update` manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when `DSH_HOME` is inside your home directory.
## Project files and git Impeccable writes its working files under `.impeccable/`. A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: `config.json`, `live/config.json`, `design.json`, `surfaces/*.md`, and `critique/*.md`. Keep `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md` in the repo too. aiSummary.oneLiner: A design guidance tool and rule detector for AI coding agents to eliminate generic frontend tropes.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Impeccable is a specialized design vocabulary and enforcement tool built to elevate the quality of frontend code generated by AI assistants. It specifically targets and eliminates common 'AI design tells'—like overused purple gradients, nested cards, and generic typography—by establishing a strict shared design context between the developer and the LLM. It initializes projects with explicit brand guidelines and provides 23 specialized commands (e.g., 'polish', 'quieter') to steer the AI's aesthetic choices. Crucially, it includes a suite of 60 deterministic, non-LLM detector rules that can instantly audit generated UI components for design flaws without requiring expensive API calls.
keyFeatures: Shared Design Context: Initialize projects with `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md` files to explicitly define brand voice, color palettes, and anti-references for the AI.
Specialized AI Commands: Utilize 23 specific directives like `audit`, `distill`, and `bolder` to precisely guide the AI's iterative design process.
Deterministic Defect Detection: Run 60 hardcoded, non-LLM rules locally to instantly catch common AI design flaws like poor contrast or inconsistent spacing.
Anti-Trope Enforcement: Actively prevent the generation of generic SaaS templates, overused gradients, and repetitive component structures.
Multi-Interface Auditing: Execute design checks seamlessly via a CLI tool against local code or through a browser extension against live websites.

useCases.title: Guiding Brand-Specific Generation
useCases.description: Use context files to ensure an AI assistant generates React components that perfectly match a company's unique aesthetic rather than a generic template.

useCases.title: Automated UI Auditing
useCases.description: Run the deterministic CLI rules against newly generated AI components to instantly identify and correct accessibility or visual hierarchy issues.

useCases.title: Iterative Design Refinement
useCases.description: Employ commands like `/impeccable critique` to force an AI coding agent to re-evaluate and improve its own layout choices before finalizing code.

useCases.title: Standardizing Team Output
useCases.description: Deploy the tool across an engineering team to ensure all AI-assisted frontend work adheres strictly to a baseline of professional design principles.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Frontend developers, designers, and engineering teams who heavily rely on AI coding assistants but require the output to be highly polished, on-brand, and structurally sound. It is designed to enforce design systems and maintain a high bar of visual quality in an automated workflow.

- **Devin and Replit Agent.** `npx impeccable install` sets the skill up for Devin on the web, in the CLI and on Desktop, and accepts `windsurf` as another name for it. A project with a `.replit` file is read as Replit Agent, so the installer names it, not Codex CLI, when it writes to `.agents`. Thanks to @faocampo and @Kodylow for asking.

- **Findings on the pull request.** In a GitHub Actions job, `impeccable detect --github` turns each finding into an annotation on the line that caused it. `--list-rules` prints every rule with its category and description, and `--scope` or `--no-advisory` narrows the list. Thanks to @mvanhorn for both.

- **A second look at hard offset shadows.** A crisp shadow pushed 4px or more is flagged as an advisory, not a failure, because it can be a deliberate neobrutalist choice. Keep one with `data-impeccable-ignore="hard-offset-shadow"`. Thanks to @mager for the contribution.

- **Cursor checks the edit it just made.** The design hook runs after each write instead of gating it, with one scan per edit. `update` and `doctor --fix` move an existing hook over.

releases.name: Skill 4.7.0
releases.body:
- **Critique and audit desktop apps.** Start an Electron, NW.js, CEF or WebView2 app with a debugging port and `impeccable detect --cdp 9222` scans the window you have open, as it stands, and leaves it exactly as it found it. Critique and audit know the recipe.

- **Two new typography checks.** `straggler` catches a paragraph that ends on one lonely word, and `unbalanced-heading` a heading whose last line is a stub. `text-wrap: balance` and `pretty` stand them down where they fix the problem.

- **Fewer false alarms on real pages.** Labels that look like buttons, card numbers, code samples that scroll, text behind curtain footers and pass-through overlays, light copy on a dark halo, and frosted glass now read the way a visitor sees them. Border accents are judged per selector, not by how many blank lines sit nearby.

- **A lighter skill.** The description that loads into every session is 30% shorter, and it now picks up requests to write a DESIGN.md or document a design system. Older command files lost their shouted CRITICAL and NEVER banners, and polish passes are no longer cut off after two rounds outside a full build.

Impeccable

The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, and catch AI slop before it ships.

From your project root:

Without Impeccable With Impeccable

Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

Why

Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md, so changes stay on-brand. More on context files.

Then name a command and a target:

/impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings

Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut.

24 commands

Commands
Steer bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects
Review critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report
Finish polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states
Iterate live live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking
Plan and set up shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system

The 24th, craft, is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs.

On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command.

Live mode

In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks.

In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent:

npx impeccable detect src/                   # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com    # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json .               # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/          # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules           # every rule with its id and description

Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173.

Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font". To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc -->. Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores.

In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay.

Installation

npx impeccable install

The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. # impeccable-ignore-end

The folders that hold decision-round state (.impeccable/questions/, .impeccable/mocks/worlds/) also ignore themselves. A .gitignore can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run git rm --cached <path>.

Good to know

Build path. For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. init asks once and saves the answer as buildPath in .impeccable/config.json; the decision page lets you override it for one session. The choice only appears when your harness can generate images. Image generation · Configuration.

Hooks run outside model approval. In Claude Code, installed command hooks run even when you deny the model's own commands, so the first edit can download the engine. Review installed hooks before unattended runs, or pass --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}' to turn them off for a run. The installer leaves hook entries it didn't add alone.

Something broken? /impeccable doctor finds stale context files, unused settings, and broken hooks. Fix setup problems.

Telemetry. When a new design starts, the skill fetches a set of visual directions from the impeccable.style catalog. Turning telemetry off doesn't stop that request; it stops the anonymous record of which directions were shown and which one you picked, which is how the catalog learns what works. Your project name, files, code, and PRODUCT.md are never sent. Disable telemetry with npx impeccable telemetry off, DO_NOT_TRACK=1, or "telemetry": false in .impeccable/config.json for the whole project. The full list of what is sent is on the privacy page.
